elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 7.3 as rendered warrants only that the Software and MarketSite.net Service "will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation" and that the media are free from defects; there is no professional-and-workmanlike performance standard for services anywhere in the amended clause.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation"; "Software" and "Documentation" are both defined terms (ss.1.10, 1.8).

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The rendered period is "ninety (90) days from the Effective Date" \u2014 the fallback floor, not the 12-month preferred duration.
The MarketSite.net Service is covered by the same conformance warranty "for a period of ninety (90) days from the Effective Date (the \"Warranty Period\")".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Retained: "Commerce One shall take all commercially reasonable efforts to correct the Software and MarketSite.net Service, or if correction ... is reasonably not possible, replace such Software and MarketSite.net Service free of charge."

Retained: "In the event any such breach of warranty can not be reasonably corrected at Commerce One's sole expense, Corio has the right to terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of all prepaid fees."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered Section 7.3; the warranty limbs are conformance to Documentation, media defects and malicious code only.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that during the Warranty Period the Software and MarketSite.net Service is free of any willfully introduced computer virus, or any other similar harmful, malicious or hidden program or data ..."

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "Software ... will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation ... for a period of ninety (90) days from the Effective Date"; the prior "but in no event not later than December 31, 1999" truncation (which would have cut the period to roughly 63 days from the 29 October 1999 Effective Date) is deleted.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: The MarketSite.net Service (the hosted service limb) is warranted under the same sentence for the full ninety (90) day Warranty Period, exceeding the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Unchanged second paragraph: correction using "all commercially reasonable efforts" and, where correction is not reasonably possible, replacement "free of charge"; defective media also replaced.

Unchanged: "Corio has the right to terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of all prepaid fees" where the breach cannot reasonably be corrected \u2014 a genuine refund limb within the standard repair/replace/refund cascade.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software conformance-to-Documentation warranty, 90-day coverage of the MarketSite.net Service (well above the 30-day floor), and retained correction/replacement plus prepaid-fee refund remedies.

Preferred level is not reached on three elements the drafter must add if pressed: (i) an express "Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" warranty, (ii) a 12-month rather than 90-day software conformance period, and (iii) a compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty. The rationale correctly notes these are not pressed.

Minimality holds. Only two edits were made inside the target element: "sixty (60)" to "ninety (90)" and deletion of the "but in no event not later than December 31, 1999" outside date. The deletion is necessary, not cosmetic \u2014 with an Effective Date of 29 October 1999 the outside date would have truncated the new 90-day period to about 63 days, so leaving it would defeat the duration element. No survival tail, expense language, extra remedies or boilerplate were added.

Intent is preserved. The defined term "Warranty Period" is retained in the same parenthetical position, so the malicious-code limb, the media-replacement sentence, the sole-and-exclusive-remedy sentence, the exclusions list and the Section 11.2 cross-reference all continue to operate without dangling references or contradiction.

Minor drafting observation only (not a defect at fallback): the period runs from the Effective Date rather than from delivery or acceptance, so it may expire before or shortly after go-live; if the deal timeline warrants, re-anchor to "from delivery" or "from the commencement of the Hosting Services" as a low-cost improvement.
